description: Check whether web features are safe to ship: Baseline state and the date it crossed, the browser and version that limits support, whether the feature is deprecated or discouraged, and the percentage points of global traffic that requiring it would exclude. Evaluates up to 20 BCD keys or web-features ids per call; up to 100 may be sent, and entries past the 20th come back unevaluated in omitted_features for the next call.

features.description: Entries to check, each a browser-compat-data key such as css.selectors.has or a web-features id such as has, 1 to 200 characters. The first 20 are evaluated per call; up to 100 are accepted, and entries past the 20th are returned unevaluated in omitted_features. More than 100 entries, or an empty or longer entry anywhere in the list, is rejected against this schema; a whitespace-only entry anywhere returns invalid_feature_input. Call browsercompat_search_features first for any entry whose key you do not already know.

resolve.description: When true, an entry that is neither a key nor an id falls back to the search index, such as "Container queries (size)" or "Element.prototype.animate". Its best exact matches are accepted only when they name one feature: a single key resolves to that key, several keys of one web-features feature resolve to the feature with its feature-level Baseline and compat_keys, and matches spanning two features are a miss. Off by default so a typo returns a miss you can correct.

name: browsercompat_check_baseline

all_widely_available.description: True only when every entry resolved and reports Baseline widely. A single miss, or any entry in omitted_features, forces false. Deprecation and discouragement do not enter this answer.

attribution.description: Required attribution for the caniuse-derived usage figures in this response.

data_version.description: Vintage of each bundled dataset behind this answer.

bcd_generated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the browser-compat-data snapshot was generated at.

browserslist.description: Version of the bundled browserslist query resolver.

caniuse_lite.description: Version of the bundled caniuse-lite snapshot.

web_features.description: Version of the bundled web-features snapshot.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_feature_input`: An entry in features is whitespace-only, including an entry past the 20th. An empty or over-200-character entry is rejected against the input schema instead. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

omitted_features.description: Entries past the first 20, verbatim and in input order, that were not evaluated. Present only when the call sent more than 20; pass them as features in the next call.

results.description: One result per evaluated entry — the first 20. A miss is a result, not a failure.

items.description: One result per evaluated entry, in input order.

baseline.description: Baseline state and the dates it crossed.

date_is_upper_bound.description: True when a date above is ≤-prefixed, so it is an upper bound rather than exact.

high_date.description: Date the feature became widely available, verbatim from web-features — may carry a ≤ prefix.

since_date.description: Date the feature became newly available, verbatim from web-features — may carry a ≤ prefix.

state.description: widely and newly are Baseline availability, limited means not yet in every core browser, not_mapped means the key sits outside the web-features mapping.

compat_keys.description: Present when the web-features id spans more than one browser-compat-data key, or as an empty list when it owns none: its first 10 keys in declaration order, with compat_keys_total counting all of them. Call browsercompat_get_feature with the id for the rest and its feature-level support per core browser, or with one of these keys for per-browser data.

compat_keys_total.description: Every browser-compat-data key the id owns. Present with compat_keys.

deprecated.description: True when browser-compat-data marks the key deprecated. Absent for keys that record no status and for ids spanning more than one key.

discouraged.description: Present when web-features records that the feature is discouraged.

according_to.description: URLs of the bodies that discourage the feature.

reason.description: Why the feature is discouraged, as web-features states it.

experimental.description: True when browser-compat-data marks the key experimental. Absent under the same conditions as deprecated.

found.description: True when the feature string resolved to a tracked entry.

guidance.description: What to do next when the feature did not resolve.

input.description: The feature string as the caller sent it.

limiting_browser.description: Among the Baseline core browsers, the one whose required release is newest by release date. For a single key, present only when every core browser has full, unprefixed, unflagged support at a resolvable added release; for an id spanning more than one key, read from web-features’ feature-level support for the feature as a whole and present only when it lists all seven core browsers.

version.description: Release of that browser the feature requires, without any ≤ prefix — see version_is_upper_bound.

version_is_upper_bound.description: True when the data says support arrived at or before version, not exactly at it. Absent when version is exact.

name.description: web-features display name for the feature.

outcome.description: found when Baseline data was returned, no_compat_data when the entry owns no browser-compat-data keys, miss when nothing matched.

baseline_id.description: The web-features id this resolved to, or null when no web-features entry covers the key.

bcd_key.description: The single browser-compat-data key this resolved to, or null when the web-features id spans more than one key or owns none.

input.description: The feature string as the caller sent it, trimmed.

resolved_via.description: Which step of the resolution order matched: bcd_key or web_features_id for an exact match, web_features_id_normalized when it matched only after lowercasing, redirect when the input pointed to a browser-compat-data entry that has moved or split, or search when resolve was true and the best exact matches in the search index all named one feature or key — treat a search match as a best guess, not a confirmed key.

resolved_as.description: How the feature string was matched, or null on a miss.

usage_percent_excluded.description: Feature-level percentage points of global traffic excluded. A resolved BCD key receives it only when it is the feature’s sole declared compat key. Absent without caniuse data — never zero in that case.

usage_source.description: What usage_percent_excluded is a share of. Present whenever that figure is.

unresolvedNotice.description: Names the entries that did not resolve and how to find the right key.

title: Browsercompat Check Baseline
